preamble.whatYouWillLearn: You will count on and back in equal steps, including fractions, decimals and negative numbers, and compare negative numbers. You will use the order of operations, so that everyone gets the same answer to a calculation, and use brackets to change that order. You will also use the laws of arithmetic to make calculations easier.
preamble.whyItMatters: Counting in equal steps helps you spot patterns and check answers. Negative numbers are used for temperatures, heights below sea level and floors below the ground. The order of operations is a rule that every calculator and spreadsheet follows, so knowing it means you get the right answer every time.
realWorld: Weather reports for cold cities, such as -5 °C in Seoul in winter
Lift buttons for basement car parks in KL malls, where B1 and B2 are like floors -1 and -2
An LRT train that arrives every 6 minutes: counting on to find when the next trains come
Working out the bill for 3 plates of nasi lemak at RM 4 and one drink at RM 2: 3 x 4 + 2 = RM 14, not RM 18
Typing a long calculation into a calculator and knowing which part it works out first

subtopics.title: Negative numbers
subtopics.summary: Read, order, and count on and back past zero, and find the difference between two temperatures on a number line.

subtopics.title: Sequences with constant steps
subtopics.summary: Count on and back in equal steps, including fractions, decimals and negative numbers, and find the term-to-term rule.

subtopics.title: Order of operations and laws of arithmetic
subtopics.summary: Work out brackets first, then multiplication and division, then addition and subtraction. Use the commutative, associative and distributive laws to make calculations easier.

questions.prompt: The thermometer shows the temperature at night. By the morning it has fallen by 5 degrees. What is the temperature in the morning?
questions.solution: The thermometer reads 3 °C. Count down 5 degrees: 2, 1, 0, -1, -2. It takes 3 steps to reach 0, then 2 more steps below zero. The morning temperature is -2 °C.

misconceptions.0: The answer is below zero, so it needs a minus sign. Counting back 5 from 3: 2, 1, 0, -1, -2.
misconceptions.1: This adds 3 and 5 and then puts a minus sign in front. Count down from 3 on the thermometer instead: you pass 0 after 3 steps and go 2 more below zero.
misconceptions.3: This adds 5 degrees. 'Fallen' means the temperature went DOWN, so count back.

questions.prompt: Which of these temperatures is the coldest?
questions.solution: On a number line, numbers further to the left are smaller. -6 is further left than -2, and -2 is left of 0. So -6 °C is the coldest.

misconceptions.1: 2 is smaller than 6, but with negative numbers it is the other way round. -2 °C is only 2 degrees below zero; -6 °C is 6 degrees below zero, which is colder.
misconceptions.2: Zero is not the lowest temperature. Negative temperatures like -2 °C and -6 °C are colder than 0 °C.

questions.prompt: Put these numbers in order from smallest to largest.
questions.solution: Think of a number line. The furthest left is -8, then -5, then -1, then 0, then 3. So the order is -8, -5, -1, 0, 3.

misconceptions.common: Putting -1 before -5 and -8 because 1 is smaller than 5 and 8. For negative numbers, the bigger the number after the minus sign, the smaller it is.

questions.prompt: True or false: -9 is greater than -4.
questions.solution: On a number line, -9 is to the left of -4, so -9 is SMALLER than -4. Think of temperatures: -9 °C is colder than -4 °C. The statement is false.

misconceptions.common: Thinking -9 is bigger because 9 is bigger than 4. -9 is further below zero, so it is smaller.

questions.prompt: The number line shows the temperature in Beijing, in °C, at 6 am and at 2 pm one day. By how many degrees did the temperature rise? Give your answer as a number of degrees.
questions.solution: Read the number line: 6 am is at -4 and 2 pm is at 7. From -4 up to 0 is 4 degrees. From 0 up to 7 is 7 degrees. Total rise: 4 + 7 = 11 degrees.

misconceptions.common: Answering 3 by working out 7 - 4. On a number line, the distance from -4 to 0 is 4 and from 0 to 7 is 7, so the rise is 4 + 7 = 11.

questions.prompt: In a shopping mall in KL, the ground floor is floor 0 and the car park floors below it are -1, -2, -3 and so on. The number line shows the floor numbers. A lift starts on floor 2, marked on the line, and goes down 5 floors. Which floor does it stop at?
questions.solution: Start at 2 on the number line and count 5 floors down: 1, 0, -1, -2, -3. The lift stops on floor -3, the third car park floor below the ground.

misconceptions.0: This counts floor 2 itself as one of the 5 steps. Count the moves: 1, 0, -1, -2, -3. That is 5 floors down.
misconceptions.1: The lift goes below the ground floor, so the floor number must be negative.
misconceptions.2: This adds 2 and 5. Going down from floor 2, you only pass 2 floors to reach 0, then 3 more below.

questions.prompt: What is the next number in this sequence? -11, -7, -3, ...
questions.solution: Each step adds 4: -11 + 4 = -7, -7 + 4 = -3. So the next number is -3 + 4 = 1. On a number line, from -3 count on 3 to reach 0, then 1 more to reach 1.

misconceptions.common: Answering -1 or -7 by counting the wrong way. The numbers are going UP by 4 each time (towards zero and past it).

questions.prompt: Count back in steps of 0.5: 1.5, 1, 0.5, 0, ... What is the next number?
questions.solution: Each step takes away 0.5. 0 - 0.5 = -0.5. On a number line, -0.5 is halfway between 0 and -1.

misconceptions.1: Counting can carry on below zero. The next number is half a step below zero, which is -0.5.
misconceptions.2: This counts back a whole 1. The step size is 0.5, so from 0 you go to -0.5.
misconceptions.3: This loses the decimal point. Half a step below zero is -0.5, not -5.

questions.prompt: The table shows the temperatures in five cities one morning. What is the difference between the highest and the lowest temperature? Give your answer as a number of degrees.
questions.solution: From the table, the highest is Penang, 31 °C. The lowest is Moscow, -12 °C (the biggest number after a minus sign). On a number line: from -12 to 0 is 12 degrees, from 0 to 31 is 31 degrees. 12 + 31 = 43 degrees.

misconceptions.common: Answering 19 by working out 31 - 12. Moscow is 12 degrees BELOW zero, so the gap is 12 degrees up to zero and then 31 more.

questions.prompt: -4 and 1 are marked with dots on the number line. Select ALL the numbers that are between -4 and 1.

diagram.alt: A number line from -6 to 3 with large marks every 1 and small marks every 0.5. Dots are drawn at -4 and at 1.

questions.solution: Look between the two dots on the number line. -3 is inside. 0 is inside. -0.5 is halfway between -1 and 0, so it is inside. -5 and -4.5 are to the left of -4. 2 is to the right of 1.

misconceptions.1: -5 is further left than -4, so it is smaller than -4 and not between -4 and 1.
misconceptions.4: 2 is bigger than 1, so it is to the right of 1.
misconceptions.5: -4.5 is half a step further left than -4, so it is smaller than -4.

questions.prompt: Look at the number line. Which number is exactly halfway between -6 and 10?

diagram.alt: A number line with -6 at the left end and 10 at the right end, and no marks in between. A box with a question mark points to the place exactly halfway between the ends.

questions.solution: The distance from -6 to 10 is 6 + 10 = 16. Half of 16 is 8. Count on 8 from -6: -6 to 0 is 6 steps, then 2 more steps reaches 2. Check: from 2 to 10 is also 8. The halfway number is 2.

misconceptions.0: 8 is half of the distance (16 ÷ 2 = 8), but you then need to count 8 on from -6, which lands on 2.
misconceptions.2: This works out -6 + 10 = 4 but forgets to halve it. The halfway point is 2.
misconceptions.3: 16 is the whole distance from -6 to 10. The halfway point is a number on the line, not a distance.

questions.skill: number line reasoning with negative numbers

questions.prompt: What is the next term in this sequence? 3, 7, 11, 15, ...
questions.solution: Find the step: 7 - 3 = 4, 11 - 7 = 4, 15 - 11 = 4. The rule is 'add 4'. The next term is 15 + 4 = 19. Well done if you checked every gap!

misconceptions.0: You added 3. Check the step: 7 - 3 = 4, so the sequence goes up by 4 each time, and 15 + 4 = 19.
misconceptions.2: You counted on by 1. The step between the terms is 4, not 1, so the next term is 15 + 4 = 19.
misconceptions.3: You doubled 15. This sequence does not multiply; it adds 4 each time, so the next term is 15 + 4 = 19.

questions.prompt: A sequence counts back in steps of 4: 10, 6, 2, ... What is the next term?
questions.solution: The rule is 'subtract 4'. From 2, count back 4 steps on a number line: 1, 0, -1, -2. So the next term is -2.

misconceptions.0: You worked out 4 - 2 instead of 2 - 4. Counting back 4 from 2 takes you past zero: 1, 0, -1, -2.
misconceptions.1: You stopped at zero. Sequences can carry on below zero into negative numbers: 2 - 4 = -2.
misconceptions.2: You added the 2 and the 4 and made it negative. Count back 4 steps from 2: 1, 0, -1, -2. The answer is -2.

questions.skill: counting on and back past zero

questions.prompt: What is the term-to-term rule for this sequence? 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4, ... Write your answer like 'add 2' or 'subtract 2'.
questions.solution: Each term is 0.5 more than the one before: 3 - 2.5 = 0.5, 3.5 - 3 = 0.5, 4 - 3.5 = 0.5. So the rule is 'add 0.5' (add a half).

misconceptions.common: Writing 'add 1' because the whole numbers 3 and 4 appear. Check the gap between every pair of terms: it is 0.5.

questions.prompt: True or false: The sequence 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 1, ... goes up in equal steps of 1/4.
questions.solution: Write every term as quarters: 1/4, 2/4, 3/4, 4/4. Each term is one more quarter, so the step is always 1/4. True!

misconceptions.common: Thinking that 1/4 to 1/2 is a bigger jump than 1/2 to 3/4. But 1/2 is the same as 2/4, so every step is 1/4.

questions.prompt: Find the missing term in this sequence: 0.7, 0.9, ___, 1.3, 1.5
questions.solution: The step is 0.9 - 0.7 = 0.2. So the missing term is 0.9 + 0.2 = 1.1. Check: 1.1 + 0.2 = 1.3, which matches the next term.

misconceptions.1: You added 9 tenths and 2 tenths and wrote 11 after the point. 11 tenths is 1 whole and 1 tenth, which is 1.1.
misconceptions.2: You counted 0.8, 0.9, 0.10 as if decimals work like whole numbers. After 0.9 comes 1.0, and 0.9 + 0.2 = 1.1.
misconceptions.3: You added 0.1. The step is 0.9 - 0.7 = 0.2, so the missing term is 0.9 + 0.2 = 1.1. Check: 1.1 + 0.2 = 1.3.

questions.prompt: At midnight the temperature on top of a high mountain is 5 °C. It falls by 3 °C every hour. What is the temperature 4 hours after midnight?
questions.solution: Count back 3 each hour: 5, 2, -1, -4, -7. After 4 hours it is -7 °C. Or: the total fall is 4 x 3 = 12 degrees, and 5 - 12 = -7.

misconceptions.0: You worked out 12 - 5 instead of 5 - 12. The temperature falls below zero, so the answer is negative: -7 °C.
misconceptions.1: You found the total fall (4 x 3 = 12 degrees) but forgot it started at 5 °C. 5 - 12 = -7.
misconceptions.3: You counted only 3 hours (5, 2, -1, -4). After 4 hours there is one more step: -4 - 3 = -7.

questions.skill: counting on and back past zero

questions.prompt: These are the first five terms of a sequence that starts at 2 and counts back in steps of 0.25, but they are mixed up. Put them in order from first term to last term.
questions.solution: Start at 2 and subtract 0.25 each time: 2, 1.75, 1.5, 1.25, 1.

misconceptions.common: Thinking 1.25 is bigger than 1.5 because 25 is bigger than 5. Compare the tenths: 1.5 has 5 tenths but 1.25 has only 2 tenths, so 1.5 is bigger and comes first.

questions.prompt: Which sequence has the term-to-term rule 'subtract 3'?
questions.solution: Check each gap. In 8, 5, 2, -1 every step is 'subtract 3': 8 - 3 = 5, 5 - 3 = 2, 2 - 3 = -1.

misconceptions.0: This sequence adds 3 each time. Subtracting makes the terms get smaller.
misconceptions.1: These are the multiples of 3. The rule is 'add 3', not 'subtract 3'.
misconceptions.3: The last step, 2 to 0, is only 2. Sequences can go below zero: 2 - 3 = -1.

questions.prompt: A sequence goes up in equal steps. The 1st term is 3/4 and the 4th term is 3. What is the 2nd term? Give your answer as a mixed number.
questions.solution: From the 1st term to the 4th term there are 3 steps. The total increase is 3 - 3/4 = 2 1/4 = 9/4. Each step is 9/4 ÷ 3 = 3/4. The 2nd term is 3/4 + 3/4 = 6/4 = 1 1/2. Check: 3/4, 1 1/2, 2 1/4, 3.

misconceptions.common: Dividing by 4 because it is the 4th term. From the 1st term to the 4th term there are only 3 jumps, so divide the increase by 3.

questions.prompt: A sequence starts at 20 and counts back in steps of 6: 20, 14, 8, ... What is the first term that is less than -10?
questions.solution: Keep subtracting 6: 20, 14, 8, 2, -4, -10, -16. -10 is not less than -10, so the first term less than -10 is -16.

misconceptions.1: -10 is in the sequence, but it is equal to -10, not less than it. The next term, -16, is the first one below -10.
misconceptions.2: -4 is the first negative term, but -4 is greater than -10. Keep counting back: -4, -10, -16.
misconceptions.3: You went one step too far. -16 is already less than -10, so it is the first one.

questions.skill: counting on and back past zero

questions.prompt: True or false: If you start at -2.5 and count on in steps of 1.5, one of the terms will be exactly 4.
questions.solution: Count on 1.5 each time: -2.5, -1, 0.5, 2, 3.5, 5, ... The terms jump from 3.5 to 5, so 4 is never a term. False.

misconceptions.common: Thinking 4 must be a term because the sequence goes past it. A sequence only lands on the numbers it steps to.

questions.skill: counting on and back past zero

questions.prompt: Work out 20 - 3 × 4.
questions.solution: Multiply before you subtract. 3 x 4 = 12. Then 20 - 12 = 8.

misconceptions.0: You worked from left to right (20 - 3 = 17, then 17 x 4 = 68). Multiplication is done before subtraction.
misconceptions.1: You worked out 3 x 4 = 12 but forgot to subtract it from 20.
misconceptions.3: You multiplied first, which is right, but then added 20 + 12 instead of subtracting.

questions.prompt: Work out (5 + 7) × 3.
questions.solution: Brackets first: 5 + 7 = 12. Then 12 x 3 = 36.

misconceptions.common: Ignoring the brackets and multiplying first: 5 + 7 x 3 = 5 + 21 = 26. Whatever is inside brackets is always worked out first.

questions.prompt: True or false: 6 × 15 = 15 × 6
questions.solution: 6 x 15 = 90 and 15 x 6 = 90. You can multiply two numbers in either order and get the same answer. This is the commutative law. The statement is true.

misconceptions.common: Thinking that changing the order changes the answer. That is true for subtraction and division (10 - 2 is not 2 - 10), but not for multiplication or addition.

questions.prompt: Which calculation gives the same answer as 7 × 48?
questions.solution: 48 = 50 - 2. So 7 x 48 = 7 x 50 - 7 x 2 = 350 - 14 = 336. Multiplying each part of a number and then combining is the distributive law.

misconceptions.1: You took 2 away only once. 48 is 50 - 2, so you need to take away seven lots of 2, which is 7 x 2 = 14.
misconceptions.2: You multiplied the 40 by 7 but forgot to multiply the 8 by 7. It should be 7 x 40 + 7 x 8.
misconceptions.3: 48 is 2 LESS than 50, so you subtract 7 x 2, not add it.

questions.prompt: Work out 25 × 37 × 4. Hint: you can multiply the numbers in any order.
questions.solution: Multiply 25 x 4 first, because it makes 100. Then 100 x 37 = 3700.

misconceptions.common: A common slip is to multiply 25 x 37 first and make a mistake on the way. With only multiplication you can choose the easiest order: 25 x 4 = 100 first, then 100 x 37 = 3700.

questions.prompt: Match each calculation to its answer.
questions.solution: 3 + 4 x 5: multiply first, 3 + 20 = 23. (3 + 4) x 5: brackets first, 7 x 5 = 35. 3 x 4 + 5: multiply first, 12 + 5 = 17. 3 x (4 + 5): brackets first, 3 x 9 = 27.

misconceptions.common: Working from left to right every time, which gives 35 for 3 + 4 x 5. Without brackets, multiplication comes before addition.

questions.prompt: Which law of arithmetic is used here?  6 × 23 = 6 × 20 + 6 × 3. Answer with one word.
questions.solution: 23 is split into 20 + 3, and each part is multiplied by 6: 120 + 18 = 138. Splitting a number into parts and multiplying each part is the distributive law.

misconceptions.common: Answering 'commutative' or 'associative'. Commutative means swapping the order (6 x 23 = 23 x 6). Associative means grouping differently ((2 x 3) x 4 = 2 x (3 x 4)).

questions.solution: Brackets first: 4 + 2 = 6. Then division and multiplication from left to right: 36 ÷ 6 = 6, then 6 x 3 = 18.

misconceptions.0: You multiplied 6 x 3 before dividing. Division and multiplication have equal priority, so after the brackets work from left to right: 36 ÷ 6 = 6, then 6 x 3 = 18.
misconceptions.1: You ignored the brackets: 36 ÷ 4 + 2 x 3 = 9 + 6 = 15. Brackets must be worked out first.
misconceptions.2: You did the brackets and the division (36 ÷ 6 = 6) but forgot to multiply by 3.

questions.prompt: Where should brackets go so that 8 + 4 × 6 - 2 equals 48?
questions.solution: Try each one. (8 + 4) x (6 - 2) = 12 x 4 = 48. This is the only one that makes 48.

misconceptions.0: This gives 12 x 6 - 2 = 72 - 2 = 70. The subtraction needs brackets too.
misconceptions.2: This gives 8 + 4 x 4 = 8 + 16 = 24. The multiplication is still done before the addition.
misconceptions.3: These brackets change nothing, because multiplication is done first anyway: 8 + 24 - 2 = 30.

questions.prompt: Work out 5 + 6 × 4.
questions.solution: Multiply before you add. 6 × 4 = 24. Then 5 + 24 = 29. The trap is working from left to right.

misconceptions.0: You worked from left to right: 5 + 6 = 11, then 11 × 4 = 44. Multiplication is done before addition, so start with 6 × 4.
misconceptions.2: You added all three numbers. The sign between 6 and 4 is ×, so multiply them: 6 × 4 = 24, then add 5.
misconceptions.3: You did 6 × 4 = 24, which is the right first step, but forgot to add the 5.

questions.prompt: Work out 30 - 12 ÷ 3.
questions.solution: Divide before you subtract. 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Then 30 - 4 = 26.

misconceptions.common: Working from left to right gives 30 - 12 = 18, then 18 ÷ 3 = 6. Division is done before subtraction, so work out 12 ÷ 3 first.

questions.prompt: True or false: 20 - 8 + 2 = 10
questions.solution: Addition and subtraction have equal priority, so work from left to right. 20 - 8 = 12. Then 12 + 2 = 14. So 20 - 8 + 2 = 14, not 10. The statement is false.

misconceptions.common: Adding first (8 + 2 = 10, then 20 - 10 = 10). Addition does not come before subtraction. When a calculation has only + and -, work from left to right.

questions.prompt: Work out 48 ÷ 4 × 2.
questions.solution: Multiplication and division have equal priority, so work from left to right. 48 ÷ 4 = 12. Then 12 × 2 = 24. The trap is multiplying first.

misconceptions.0: You multiplied 4 × 2 = 8 first, then 48 ÷ 8 = 6. Multiplication does not come before division. When there is only × and ÷, work from left to right.
misconceptions.1: You did 48 ÷ 4 = 12, which is right, but stopped there. You still need to multiply by 2.
misconceptions.3: You did 48 ÷ 4 = 12, then added 2 instead of multiplying by 2. Check each sign before you use it.

questions.prompt: Aisha buys 3 plates of nasi lemak at RM 6 each and 2 cups of teh tarik at RM 4 each. Which calculation gives the total cost in ringgit? Choose one.
questions.solution: The nasi lemak costs 3 × 6 = RM 18. The teh tarik costs 2 × 4 = RM 8. Add them: 18 + 8 = RM 26. In one calculation this is 3 × 6 + 2 × 4, because the multiplications are done first. The trap is adding the plates and cups together: they have different prices.

misconceptions.1: This adds the plates and cups (3 + 2 = 5) and adds the prices (6 + 4 = 10), giving RM 50. But a cup does not cost RM 10. Each item must be multiplied by its own price first.
misconceptions.2: This gives 18 + 2 + 4 = RM 24. It adds RM 2 and RM 4 instead of working out 2 cups at RM 4 each. The cups need 2 × 4.
misconceptions.3: This gives 3 × 8 × 4 = RM 96. The brackets add a price to a number of cups, which does not make sense. Find the cost of each kind of item, then add.

questions.prompt: Select ALL the calculations that give the same answer as 8 × 7 × 5.
questions.solution: When you only multiply, you can change the order (commutative law) and the grouping (associative law). 8 × 5 × 7 swaps the order. 8 × 5 = 40, so 40 × 7 works. 7 × 5 = 35, so 8 × 35 works. All three give 280. 8 × 7 + 5 = 61 and 13 × 7 = 91, so they do not.

misconceptions.1: 8 × 7 + 5 = 56 + 5 = 61. Changing × to + changes the answer. Only the order and grouping of the multiplications can change.
misconceptions.4: 13 × 7 comes from adding 8 + 5 = 13. But 8 and 5 are multiplied, not added: 8 × 5 = 40, so it should be 40 × 7.
misconceptions.common: Remember: with only multiplication you may swap the numbers round or multiply any pair first, but you must not change a × into a +.

questions.prompt: Omar types 60 - 24 ÷ 4 + 2 into a calculator that uses the order of operations. Omar says: "It will show 11, because 60 - 24 = 36, 36 ÷ 4 = 9 and 9 + 2 = 11." Is Omar correct? Choose the answer with the correct reason.
options: Yes. A calculator works from left to right, so it shows 11.
No. It divides first, then adds before it subtracts: 60 - 8 = 52.
No. It divides first, so it shows 60 - 6 = 54.
questions.solution: Division comes before addition and subtraction: 24 ÷ 4 = 6. That leaves 60 - 6 + 2. Now work from left to right: 60 - 6 = 54, then 54 + 2 = 56. The calculator shows 56, so Omar is not correct. His mistake was working from left to right.

misconceptions.0: This is Omar's mistake. A calculator that uses the order of operations divides before it adds or subtracts: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 comes first.
misconceptions.1: You divided first, which is right, but then added 6 + 2 before subtracting. + and - have equal priority, so work from left to right: 60 - 6 = 54, then 54 + 2 = 56.
misconceptions.2: You divided first and subtracted correctly, but forgot the + 2 at the end. Use every part of the calculation: 54 + 2 = 56.

questions.prompt: Select ALL the calculations that equal 20.
questions.solution: Work out each one with the order of operations. 2 + 3 × 4 = 2 + 12 = 14. 40 ÷ 4 × 2 = 10 × 2 = 20. 50 - 20 + 10 = 30 + 10 = 40. 4 + 4 × 4 = 4 + 16 = 20. 30 - 5 × 2 = 30 - 10 = 20. 80 ÷ 2 × 2 = 40 × 2 = 80. So three calculations equal 20. Check every option before you answer.

misconceptions.0: 2 + 3 × 4 is 14, not 20. Working from left to right gives 5 × 4 = 20, but the multiplication must be done first: 2 + 12 = 14.
misconceptions.2: 50 - 20 + 10 is 40, not 20. You probably added 20 + 10 first. With only + and -, work from left to right: 50 - 20 = 30, then 30 + 10 = 40.
misconceptions.5: 80 ÷ 2 × 2 is 80, not 20. You probably multiplied 2 × 2 first. With only × and ÷, work from left to right: 80 ÷ 2 = 40, then 40 × 2 = 80.
misconceptions.common: Work out every calculation in full before you choose. Multiply and divide before you add and subtract; when the signs have equal priority, go from left to right.

questions.prompt: Work out 4 × (9 - 2).
questions.solution: Brackets first: 9 - 2 = 7. Then 4 × 7 = 28.

misconceptions.common: Ignoring the brackets: 4 × 9 - 2 = 36 - 2 = 34. Whatever is inside the brackets is always worked out first.

questions.prompt: Match each calculation to the working that gives the same answer.
questions.solution: Split the bigger number and multiply each part (the distributive law). 6 × 47 = 6 × 40 + 6 × 7 = 240 + 42 = 282. 8 × 39 = 8 × 40 - 8 × 1 = 320 - 8 = 312. 5 × 64 = 5 × 60 + 5 × 4 = 300 + 20 = 320. The trap: every part must be multiplied, not just the tens.

misconceptions.common: Choosing 6 × 40 + 7 or 8 × 40 - 1. These multiply only one part of the number. In 6 × 47, the 7 must also be multiplied by 6: 6 × (40 + 7) = 6 × 40 + 6 × 7.

questions.prompt: Kumar has RM 50. He buys 4 durian puffs at RM 3 each and one drink for RM 5. Which calculation gives the money he has left, in ringgit?
questions.solution: He spends 4 × 3 = RM 12 on puffs and RM 5 on the drink, so 12 + 5 = RM 17 altogether. The brackets show that all of this is taken from RM 50: 50 - (4 × 3 + 5) = 50 - 17 = RM 33. The trap: without brackets, the drink is added back on.

misconceptions.0: Without brackets this is 50 - 12 + 5 = RM 43. The RM 5 is added back, as if Kumar was given money for the drink. Both costs must be taken away, so put them in brackets.
misconceptions.2: This takes 4 from RM 50 first, which is not a cost in the story, and gives RM 143, more than he started with. The 4 is a number of puffs, so it belongs with the price: 4 × 3.
misconceptions.3: This gives 50 - 4 × 8 = RM 18, as if he bought a drink with every puff. He bought only one drink.

questions.prompt: Siti wants 36 ÷ 3 + 3 × 2 to equal 12. She may add one pair of brackets. Which calculation equals 12?
questions.solution: Work out each one. 36 ÷ (3 + 3) × 2: brackets first, 36 ÷ 6 = 6, then 6 × 2 = 12. (36 ÷ 3 + 3) × 2 = 15 × 2 = 30. 36 ÷ (3 + 3 × 2) = 36 ÷ 9 = 4. (36 ÷ 3) + 3 × 2 = 12 + 6 = 18. Only the first equals 12. Trap: after the brackets, work ÷ and × from left to right; do not multiply 6 × 2 first.

misconceptions.2: Inside the brackets, multiply first: 3 + 3 × 2 = 3 + 6 = 9. Then 36 ÷ 9 = 4, not 12.
misconceptions.3: These brackets go round a part that is worked out first anyway, so they change nothing: 12 + 6 = 18.
